scope: Go struct field and interface element owners: field slots for the names of a field declaration, node owners for an embedded field, a method element and a name-led type element; Unit 2 of #1672

reference.configuration: go/parser.ParseFile with ParseComments|AllErrors|SkipObjectResolution on each source as one file; ast.Field Doc and Comment per struct field and interface element, with names and byte offsets; go/doc.NewFromFiles with AllDecls|AllMethods|PreserveAST for sources without a parse error. Run under env -i with GOPROXY=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOENV=off and every cache inside the run directory
reference.evidence: Executed on 2026-11-25 for every source of the production oracles; the Doc group of each field and element, its names and the extent of each member were compared with the expected owners. Also for 1,948 generated sources with a line end at every gap of 99 member forms, and for 2,031 files of the Go 1.26.1 standard library, read only
reference.qualification: Source attachment only. No gofmt, go vet or type check; publication is not claimed.

legacy_measurement.binary: bca 2.6.1 built from the base commit, debug profile
legacy_measurement.qualification: Each measured file holds exactly the bytes of one legacy oracle source: no CR and one final LF, so file normalization changes nothing.

known_differences:
A member whose children include a comment with a line break stays a pending owner. Go ends a line at such a comment: for X /* a
 b */ int it reads two embedded fields, and for M() /* a
 b */ int a method and an embedded element. Where the comment follows a comma, a bar or a star, Go reads what the grammar reads and the member is pending all the same.

A member that Go ends at a line end before the end of its node stays a pending owner. Go puts a semicolon at a line end after an identifier, a literal, ), ] or }, also where a comment ends the line; the pinned grammar reads some members on past it. X [2]
int is one field for the grammar and two embedded fields for Go; X func() /* a
 b */ int is one field for the grammar, and a field and an embedded field for Go.

The members between the braces of a nested struct or interface type are read on their own. In a file Go rejects, a member can have its owners inside or around a member that stays pending (X [2]
struct { A int }).
A field of a struct declared in a function body, and an element of an interface declared there, has no owner and its comment is no document; go/ast attaches the comment as Doc.
A member with a syntax error of its own stays a pending owner; go/parser recovers and attaches the comment.

A member without an error of its own gets its owners beside an ERROR node. An unclosed method M( is read by the pinned grammar as a type element M, which owns the comment; a function after an unclosed struct is read as an embedded field.

The pinned grammar accepts a line feed inside a field type where Go ends the line and rejects the file (X map[string]
int); the field stays a pending owner.
The local text of // a is a; CommentGroup.Text returns a with a final line feed.

The pinned grammar reads a form feed and a vertical tab as white space, and Go rejects both bytes. A member with one of them between two of its tokens (X [2] int) keeps its owners as the grammar reads.
